newsitem.title: FRANCE: DF1-Premiere accord possible, says Kirch aide.
newsitem.headline: DF1-Premiere accord possible, says Kirch aide.

text.p: An accord between German television channels DF1 and Premiere is on the cards, but Leo Kirch, owner of DF1, is in no hurry to find a partner, Kirch aide Jan Mojito said in an interview with French daily Le Monde.
"We are neither in a hurry nor obliged to find one. If we conclude a partnership, we want to remain leader in the operation," he said in the interview published on Tuesday afternoon.
Mojito also said that an accord was near at Italy's Telepiu, owned by Nethold, now part of France's Canal Plus, Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest and Kirch.
He confirmed that DF1 costs Kirchgruppe, Bavarian media magnate Leo Kirch's company, nearly a billion marks a year.
"But we do not lack German or foreign banks to finance our broadcasting activities," Mojito said.

An agreement between digital television service DF1 and analogue pay television channel Premiere, which is 37.5 percent owned each by Canal Plus and Germany's Bertelsmann and 25 percent by Kirch, is envisaged, Mojito said.
"These decisions have to be approved by the three shareholders," he said.

"The idea is to create clear majorities at the channels, at a time when we need to move forward. Several possibilities are being looked at in Premiere. Either Kirch or CLT-UFA (Bertelsmann's broadcasting division) get the majority, or a strict equality between the three shareholders could be sought," he said.
"The problem seems less complex within Telepiu, where we are close to an accord, but the time scale is a bit complicated," he said.
Mojito also confirmed that German public channel ZDF plans to buy programmes worth 200 million marks from Kirchgruppe.
